media_strategy.selection_principle: Data-driven. This is an analytical financial time-series, so charts carry the argument; one atmospheric hero image sets tone; one guess-first interactive and one chart-synced sonification add embodiment. Video and stock imagery would be decorative for a financials story, so they are deliberately limited per the LEAN budget.

chart.reason: The dataset is quantitative time-series; charts are the primary evidence vehicle.

image.reason: One generated hero image conveys the flat-then-vertical 'cliff' emotionally before the data does. LEAN budget = exactly one image.

video.reason: A financials time-series has no event/process to animate; per the LEAN media budget no video is generated. The hero image and charts carry the visual load.

audio.reason: A 16-point ordered revenue sequence is exactly the kind of small ranked series sonification handles well — the reader can hear the flat decade then the vertical spike, synced to the revenue chart. Web Audio API only, no generated/embedded file needed.

interactive_or_map.reason: No geography, so the interactive is a guess-first reveal on the net-income scale jump plus a chart-synced sonification scrubber, turning surprising findings into participation.

des_00.label: Teaser hero image — the cliff

content.prompt: A cinematic abstract data visualization: a near-vertical glowing green ascending line erupting from a long flat baseline on a deep matte-black background, like a financial chart turning into a cliff face of light, faint silicon-wafer circuitry texture etched in the dark, volumetric haze, dramatic single light source, editorial finance magazine cover aesthetic, no text, no numbers, no logos, ultra high detail

des_00.brief: Full-viewport teaser. The generated abstract 'cliff of light' image fills the screen with no prose, only a faint scroll cue at the bottom. The image visually previews the flat-then-vertical revenue shape before any number appears. Dark, cinematic, restrained.
des_00.rationale: The whole story is a shape — flat then vertical. A single atmospheric image lets the reader feel that shape before the charts prove it. One image only, per the LEAN budget.

des_01.label: Revenue trajectory line chart (the cliff)

highlight.note: mark the inflection at the fiscal year ending Jan 2024

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows fy_end_year, revenue_b, and rev_yoy_pct

style.palette: single accent green #76b900 line on dark

des_01.brief: A single line of annual revenue ($B) from FY-end 2011 to 2026, NVIDIA-green on a dark panel. The line is visibly flat through ~2016 then bends sharply upward after 2023. Add a vertical reference rule + annotation at fy_end_year 2024 labeled 'the cliff'. Points are dots; hover reveals exact revenue and YoY %. width:container.
des_01.rationale: A line chart is the only honest way to show the flat-then-vertical shape; bars would obscure the slope change. This is the section that must make the cliff self-evident.

des_02.label: Hinge bar chart — top YoY growth years

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows revenue_b and rev_yoy_pct

des_02.brief: Horizontal or vertical bar chart of the top-5 YoY revenue growth years (FY-end 2024 +125.9%, 2025 +114.2%, 2026 +65.5%, 2022 +61.4%, 2021 +52.7%), sorted descending. The FY-end 2024 bar is the brightest/highlighted to mark the hinge. Hover shows the absolute revenue too.
des_02.rationale: After the line chart, a ranked bar gives a different visual mode (no chart streak) and isolates just how extreme the inflection year was relative to NVIDIA's own history.

des_03.label: Hero / chapter-break image (reuse) for the hinge

content.prompt: (reused teaser image) abstract green cliff-of-light over a flat baseline on matte black

des_03.brief: Reuse the same hero.png as a full-width chapter-break image inside the hinge section, between the 'bad year' paragraph and the 'hinge turned' paragraph, to give the turn an emotional beat. No new asset generated — same file, per LEAN budget.
des_03.rationale: The editor flagged [MEDIA: image] here. Reusing the single hero image as a chapter divider honors the LEAN one-image budget while still giving the turn a visual punctuation.

des_04.label: Margins layered line chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows both margins for the year

style.palette: gross margin light green, net margin amber

des_04.brief: Two lines on one panel: gross margin and net margin (%), FY-end 2011-2026. Net margin shows the sharp V-dip at FY-end 2023 (16.2%) — annotate it. Gross margin steps up above 70% from FY-end 2024. Two-color legend, hover tooltip with both values.
des_04.rationale: Layering both margins shows the FY2023 scar and the new 70%+ gross-margin tier in one view; the V-dip is the visual hook.

des_05.label: Net income guess-first interactive

content.initial_state: A prompt: 'NVIDIA earned $0.25B in profit in FY2011. Guess its FY2026 net income.' Reader sees a slider (0 to $150B) or three multiple-choice chips ($20B / $60B / $120B) with a tiny flat-then-rising sparkline.
content.trigger: Reader moves the slider / picks a chip and clicks Reveal
content.transition: The full net-income bar chart (FY-end 2011-2026) animates in, bars growing from baseline, with the reader's guess shown as a dashed line for comparison
content.payoff: Reveal $120.07B (a 474x increase) and the FY-end 2024 jump from $4.37B; most readers will have guessed far too low

des_05.brief: Guess-first reveal. Reader commits to a guess for FY2026 net income, then the animated bar chart of net income ($B) by FY-end year appears with their guess overlaid as a dashed reference line and the actual $120.07B / 474x highlighted. Must work as a plain bar chart with a visible affordance (chips + Reveal button); the chart uses ana_04's data_table.
des_05.rationale: Editor flagged [MEDIA: interactive]. The 474x figure is so large that letting readers guess first maximizes the surprise — far stronger than a passive chart, and it breaks the chart rhythm.

des_06.label: EPS trap dual chart (EPS vs net income)

highlight.note: EPS falls while net income more than doubles

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows both eps_diluted and net_income_b

style.palette: EPS in red/coral (the misleading line), net income in green (the truth)

des_06.brief: Side-by-side / dual-axis comparison for FY-end 2024-2026: a coral EPS series that visibly DROPS from 11.93 to 2.94, next to a green net-income series ($B) that RISES from 29.76 to 72.88 to 120.07. Annotate the contradiction: 'EPS down 75%, profit up 145% — the 10:1 split is why.' Two separate y-axes, clearly labeled, with a caption that raw EPS and price must never share an axis.
des_06.rationale: The whole point of the section is the visual contradiction between two series; placing the falling EPS bar next to the rising net-income bar makes the trap instantly legible.

des_07.label: Price vs revenue vs net income dual-axis chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows price, revenue_b, net_income_b for the year

style.palette: price white/teal, revenue green, net income muted gold

des_07.brief: Three lines, two y-axes: split-adjusted price ($) on the left axis, revenue and net income ($B) on the right. All three share the same flat-then-vertical shape. Annotate the FY-end 2024 point where price ($60.99) and revenue ($60.92B) nearly coincide. Caption notes the 0.991/0.992 correlation. Hover shows all three values.
des_07.rationale: Showing price and fundamentals on the same time axis (different scales) makes the 0.99 correlation visible as parallel lines, setting up the re-rating reveal in the next section.

des_08.label: Indexed re-rating chart (log scale)

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows revenue_index and price_index

style.fill_gap: subtle shaded band between the two lines

des_08.brief: Two lines indexed to FY-end 2011 = 100 on a LOG y-axis so both fit: revenue index and price index. The price line sits well above revenue from ~2017 on and ends at 34,752 vs 6,094 — shade the widening gap between them to dramatize the re-rating. Log scale is essential or the early years collapse to zero. Hover shows both index values.
des_08.rationale: Indexing + log scale is the cleanest way to show that price compounded faster than revenue despite the 0.99 correlation — the gap between the lines IS the valuation re-rating.

des_09.label: Annual returns diverging bar chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows year and yoy_return_pct

style.palette: green for positive returns, red for negative

des_09.brief: Diverging bar chart of calendar-year stock returns since 2011: green bars above zero, red bars below. The +239% (2023) and +227% (2016) bars tower; the -50% (2022) and -31% (2018) bars plunge below the zero line. Explicit zero baseline. Hover shows exact %. Shows the violent volatility under the upward trend.
des_09.rationale: A diverging bar chart makes the up-and-down whipsaw obvious in a way the smooth price line cannot — the right closing visual for 'never a smooth ride'.

des_10.label: R&D intensity stat callout

content.label: of revenue now goes to R&D — a record $18.5B in dollars, down from a 32% peak

des_10.brief: Large 64px stat: '8.6%' with the label below explaining it is a record $18.5B in absolute terms yet the lowest R&D-to-revenue ratio ever — the signature of extreme operating leverage. Centered, with vertical spacing.
des_10.rationale: ana_06 is color, not a full chart-worthy section; a single stat callout lands the operating-leverage point without adding another chart to the closing section.

des_11.label: Revenue sonification — hear the cliff

content.why_audio: Mapping the 16 annual revenue values to ascending pitch lets the reader HEAR the flat decade as a near-constant low drone then the sudden vertical leap as a rapid pitch climb — the same shape the eye sees in des_01, reinforced through a second sense.
content.trigger: Click a 'Play the revenue curve' button beneath the revenue line chart (des_01). Never autoplay.
content.ui_form: chart-synced sonification: as each year's tone plays, the matching point on the des_01 line chart highlights and a year/value label updates

content.legend: Higher pitch = higher revenue; each note is one fiscal year, 2011 -> 2026.

content.fallback: If Web Audio is unavailable or muted, the des_01 line chart fully communicates the same shape; the play button shows a disabled tooltip.
content.novelty_note: Not a standalone tone card — the tones are bound to the revenue line chart and only meaningful while watching the point highlight move across the cliff.

des_11.brief: A click-to-play sonification of the 16 annual revenue values (ana_01.data_table revenue_b), mapped log-pitch onto a triangle oscillator, 320ms per note, synced so the corresponding point on the des_01 revenue chart lights up as each note plays. Includes a tiny legend ('higher pitch = more revenue') and a mute-respecting visual fallback.
des_11.rationale: Editor used a chart in edt_01; sonification adds a non-decorative audio channel that genuinely re-encodes the lead finding (the cliff shape) for a second sense, satisfying the data-driven audio default without a generic tone card.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial, finance-magazine restraint with a single NVIDIA-green accent
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-then-visual; each section states the finding in prose, then proves it with a chart/interactive directly below
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoid a chart-after-chart monotony by alternating modes: line (des_01) -> bar (des_02) -> dual-line margins (des_04) -> guess-first interactive (des_05) -> dual-axis EPS-vs-profit (des_06) -> price/fundamentals (des_07) -> log-indexed re-rating (des_08) -> diverging returns bar (des_09) + stat callout (des_10). The sonification (des_11) and one reused hero image are the only non-chart media, kept lean and data-bound rather than decorative.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large stat callout at 64px; section titles in system-ui caps with green underline accents; body in Georgia serif; pull the EPS-trap caption out as an italic warning. Dark background (#0b0b0d) with #76b900 accent.
